nodes.description: After more than twenty years of chronic pyothorax, usually following artificial pneumothorax for pulmonary tuberculosis or tuberculous pleuritis, an Epstein-Barr virus-associated diffuse large B-cell lymphoma can arise in the pleural cavity. Chronic inflammatory cytokines and reactive oxygen species are proposed contributors. Pyothorax-associated lymphoma is reported almost entirely from Japan; it is a late complication of the chronic pyothorax rather than of tuberculous empyema in general.

evidence.reference_title: Pyothorax-associated lymphoma: a lymphoma developing in chronic inflammation.
evidence.snippet: Pyothorax-associated lymphoma (PAL) is a non-Hodgkin lymphoma of exclusively B-cell phenotype developing in the pleural cavity of patients after more than 20-year history of pyothorax resulting from an artificial pneumothorax for the treatment of pulmonary tuberculosis or tuberculous pleuritis.

evidence.reference_title: Pyothorax-associated lymphoma: a lymphoma developing in chronic inflammation.
evidence.snippet: Use of an artificial pneumothorax, EBV infection, and cytokines and reactive oxygen species produced in longstanding pyothorax might be important factors for PAL development.

nodes.description: Artificial pneumothorax, thoracoplasty and related collapse therapies, used for cavitary pulmonary tuberculosis before effective chemotherapy, are a historical, now rare, cause of chronic tuberculous empyema and the setting in which pyothorax-associated lymphoma later develops. nodes.description: Surgical removal of the pleural peel to re-expand a trapped lung, by thoracotomy or video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery, including uniportal VATS for stage III disease. Large Chinese series report no perioperative deaths and high rates of full re-expansion, with prolonged air leak the commonest complication; drug-resistant disease makes surgery harder and raises complications. Operating after more than six weeks of chemotherapy gave better re-expansion than earlier surgery in one prospective comparison.
